page: Microsoft Azure E192ids_v6 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server features 1832.0 GB of system memory, yielding 9.54 GB of RAM per core. It is equipped with 11339 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is premium storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 158923.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21589.0. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 12329.57 GB/sec for small block cached reads and 430.1 GB/sec for large block uncached reads. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and gzip compression benchmarks placing in the average tier. However, multi-threaded workloads like bzip3 decompression at 941.18 GB/sec and Passmark database operations at 35481.69 rank in the top tier. The system also demonstrates strong capabilities in LLM inference for medium 7B models, achieving 240.31 tokens/sec for prompt processing.

Given its massive memory capacity, high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and dense 192-vCPU configuration, the E192ids_v6 offers high resource density for enterprise-scale workloads. The qualitative tradeoff involves high multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth at the expense of average single-core efficiency. This hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, heavy data processing, software compilation, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
